title: No skill catalog or trigger index: 42 in-repo and 315 installed skills, 71% without a loadable trigger, none owned
reasoning: Borrowed from rlaope/oh-my-hermes src/skills/catalog.py, which ships 418 indexed skills with categories and triggers; the mechanism is worth copying, the library is not. Skills are the cheapest capability amplification the fleet has and they are currently undiscoverable: discovery is the description prefix, and 71% of ours fail it. Measured 2026-10-28 across ~/coding-hermes-skills (42 SKILL.md, 12 trigger-compliant, 3 empty, 6 over length) and ~/.hermes/skills (315 skills, 81 compliant, 94 over length, 11 with triggers[], 13 with tags, 0 with owner). Without a catalog nobody can answer which skills are used, which are dead, or which project owns each one.
acceptance_criteria: The runtime only sees a skill through the first 57 characters of its description, yet only 12 of 42 repo skills and 81 of 315 installed skills open with a real 'Use when <trigger>.' sentence; three repo descriptions are empty, six exceed 200 chars, 94 installed ones do, and not one skill anywhere declares an owner. So most of the fleet's procedural memory is reachable only by guessing its name. Deliver a generated catalog from SKILL.md frontmatter (never hand-maintained): name, first-57-char trigger, owner, category, project scope, last-use evidence, and a task-to-skill lookup so selection is a query rather than a memory exercise. Enforce the contract at write time - a guard fails any skill added without a front-loaded trigger and an owner, and fails an empty description. Add an owner to every existing skill, derived from the repo or lane that maintains it, listing whatever cannot be attributed. Count skill_view loads per skill from state.db and publish the most-loaded and never-loaded lists so dead skills get merged or retired. Do NOT import oh-my-hermes 418-skill library.
acceptance: A generated catalog exists with zero hand-maintained fields; a guard fails a new skill lacking a 57-char trigger or an owner; every skill carries an owner or is explicitly listed as unattributable; usage counts exist per skill with never-loaded named; repo description defects (3 empty, 6 over length) are zero; a task-vocabulary lookup returns candidate skills for a sample of 10 real fleet tasks.
